r2_body: 47I dranke, and ſhe watered the cammels. † And I asked her, and ſaid : Whoſe daughter arr thou who anſwered: I am the daughter of Bathuel, the ſonne of Nachor, whom Melcha bare him. I hoong therfore earclettes to adone her ſace, and I put braceletts vpon her hands. † And pro- ſtrate I adored our Lord, bleſſing the Lord God of my lord Abraham, who hath broughr me the ſtraight way to take the daughter of my lords brother for his ſonne. † Wher- fore if you doe according to mercie and truth with mv lord, ſew me: but if it pleaſe you otherwiſe, that alſo tel me, that I may goe to the right hand, or to the left. † And Laban and Bathuel anſwered: From our Lord the word hath proceded : we can not ſpeake any other thing with thee beſides his pleaſure. † Behold Rebecca is before thee, take her and goe thy waies, and let her be the wife of thy lords ſonne, as our Lord hath ſpoken. † Which when A- brahams ſeruant heard, falling downe he adored our Lord to the grounde. † And taking forth veſſel of ſiluer, and gold, and garments, gaue them to Rebecca for a preſent. To her brothers alſo, and to her mother he offred giftes. † A banket was made, and eating and drinking togeather they lodged there. And in the morning, the ſeruant aroſe, and ſaid : Diſmiſſe me, that I may goe to my lord. † And : As children her brother, and mother anſwered : Let the maide rarie at ought not to the leaſt tenne days with vs, and after ſhe ſhal depart. † Stay me not, ſaid he, becauſe our Lord hath directed my way : gond liking- diſmiſſe me that I may goe on to my lord. † And they ſaid : ſo the parties Let vs cal the maid, and aske her wil. † And being called, owne conſent when ſhe was come, they asked : Wilt thou goe with this is moſt neceſ- man? who ſaid : I wil goe. † They diſmiſſed her therfore, and her nurce, and Abrahams ſeruant, and his companie, Epiſt † wiſhing proſpericie to their ſiſter, and ſaying : Thou art: Suach ſigni- our ſiſter, encreaſe thou into rhouſand thouſands, and thy ſieth to ſpeake ſeed poſſeſſe the gates of theirenemies † Therfore Rebecca, conſideratly and her maides being ſet vpon camels, folowed the man who with ſpeed returned vnto his lord, and † the ſame s. Ambroſe rime Iſa ic walked along the wav, that leadeth to the wel (l c. de of the Liuing and the ſeing, ſo called: for he dwelt in the Iſaac and s. ſouth countrie: † and he was gone forth to : meditate in the field, the day nowe being wel ſpent : and when he had derſtand it of caſt vp his eyes, he ſaw camels coming a farre of. † Rebecca mental prayer
